ACTION 16 OF 32 · PHASE 04

Ask whether this can grow past the first island

Differentiate a repeatable profitable model from an expensive expansion idea.

WHEN TO DO THISBefore promising a regional footprint or investing in multi-country infrastructure.ESTIMATED WORK TIME45 min
↗
Your one job

Differentiate a repeatable profitable model from an expensive expansion idea.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    Break the service into central functions and island-specific functions.

  2. 02

    List geography-specific constraints: payments, regulation, insurance, people, suppliers, taxes, shipping and support.

  3. 03

    Compare partner/licensing/white-label models against owning local operations.

  4. 04

    Choose one smaller replication experiment; set cost, margin and stop conditions.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Assess whether this business can scale from [HOME MARKET] to two realistic target Caribbean markets. Compare centralized operations, local partners, licensing, white-label and direct expansion. For each scenario list actual dependencies to verify, likely unit-economics changes, regulations to research, operational risks and the smallest reversible pilot. Do not assert market presence or legal eligibility without proof.
03

Finish with this

A scale map: what stays centralized, what must localize, and the cheapest expansion test.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • Home-market delivery works or limitations are acknowledged
  • One candidate market and pilot defined
  • Expansion costs/partners not assumed free
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

Building island selectors for a service you haven't proven on the first island.

READY TO MOVE ON?

Price exceeds variable costs, capacity and cash needs are realistic, and at least one acquisition path can plausibly work.
